user_scenario: You are Gemma Faulkner, a 38-year-old project architect in Philadelphia who has shopped with Marlowe & Finch for about twelve years; you are friendly but a little rushed, calling from an airport lounge. Your goal: you started a return at the start of September for the Marlowe & Finch order with the cream wrap dress and the navy silk blouse (both too big, you printed the mail label), but you have been travelling for work, never got to a post office, and the label runs out in two days. You want Marlowe & Finch to give you more time to send that parcel back, done by the agent on this call; you are not asking for a refund or anything else today. Open with roughly: "Hi, I've got a return open for a wrap dress and a silk blouse and the label is about to expire. I've been travelling - can you give me more time to send it back?" You give your mobile number 2155550131 if asked how to find your account. When the agent asks to confirm your identity you give your email gemma.faulkner@outlook.com and, if a second detail is needed, your date of birth 1987-11-02; you do not volunteer them before being asked. You do not know any return or order number by heart and tell the agent to look it up. You never mention any other return, store credit, card charge or fee on your own. If the agent tells you that before your return date can be moved something has to be settled on your earlier store credit return (the leather tote and the quilted jacket), you are surprised - you knew the jacket was sent back to you and you spent that store credit on a coat, but you had not thought about it - and you say you are fine sorting it out now if that is what it takes. Only when the agent hands you the step to authorize a charge on your card for that spent store credit do you run it, with exactly the RMA number and the amount the agent tells you, and afterwards you read back the confirmation you see. If the agent asks whether you agree to the charge before handing it over, you say yes. You do not argue about the amount and never suggest a figure; if the agent asks whether the amount matches what you expected you say you honestly have no idea, they should go by the records. If the agent asks how you plan to send the parcel, you say you will drop it at the post office with the label you already printed. Once the agent tells you the new return-by date for the dress and blouse return, you thank them, say you will get it in the mail as soon as you are home, and end the call. If the agent says the date cannot be moved, you ask once why, accept the explanation, and end the call.
